Login is the best screen in the product and sets an expectation the app cannot keep. `app/login/page.tsx:37-54` gives her a full-bleed dark stage, a 56px Cormorant hero split across two lines with the italic gold second line, a Brontë epigraph pulled from a real Gutenberg source with a "Read the source" link, and a single quiet card on the right. It is confident, literary, unhurried. She will like it. Then she signs in and lands on `connected-home.tsx`. The hero still holds — "Welcome home, Cassandra." in the same serif, the quote carried over. Below it, three things go wrong in the first screenful. The right-hand "Cassandra's Desk" card is stretched to the height of the inspiration card next to it (`app/globals.css:2877` `.connected-main-grid` has no `align-items:start`), and `app/globals.css:2979` pins its button with `margin-top:auto`, so roughly 300px of pure void sits between "Your desk is clear" and "Add an idea or request." It reads as a rendering failure, not as air. Immediately under it, the one row of hard numbers on her home page says **08 · 00 · 00 · 00** in 45px Cormorant (`app/globals.css:2862`), with its explanatory captions set at 9px (`app/globals.css:2871`). Her first impression of her own workspace is three large zeros. And the supporting prose on that same card is 11px (`app/globals.css:2962`) — so the page swings from 45px to 11px to 9px with nothing in between. Her first click is the likeliest problem. The sidebar offers "Marketing Plans — Goals, review & your next steps" with a target icon, one item above "Ask Raven." In demo mode `plans-page.tsx:41` returns `

If Michael demos in demo mode, that is a hole in the floor. scores.verdict: Three or four surfaces (login, universe catalog, demo mission control, the book covers) are the work of someone with real taste. The system underneath them does not exist: 532 distinct hex values against 123 token references, 48 distinct font sizes down to 3px, every integer from 1–36px used as spacing, 14 breakpoints, 10 border-radii while four radius tokens sit unused, and five different checkbox accent colors. The result is that care is distributed by page rather than by system, so /plans, /opportunities, /studio and connected settings look like a different product than / and /universe.

top_findings.title: /plans in demo mode renders with no styling at all — `.page-stack` is defined in zero stylesheets
top_findings.problem:
The demo fallback returns `

Marketing Plans

…

Back to the desk
`. I grepped every CSS file in the repo for `page-stack` and it is defined nowhere, so the page has no container, no spacing, no max-width. The `` carries no class, so it renders as plain body-coloured text with no underline and no button — indistinguishable from the paragraph above it. Marketing Plans is a top-level sidebar item with an inviting description, one slot above Ask Raven, and demo is the mode most likely to be shown tomorrow. desktop-plans.png confirms: three lines of raw HTML on an empty 1400px canvas.
top_findings.proposed_change: Use the standard page shell — `.page-heading` with eyebrow + h1 + subtitle + a 32px icon, then a `<Card className="settings-card">` explaining that plans live in the connected workspace, with `<Button asChild variant="outline"><Link href="/desk">Back to the desk <ArrowRight size={15} /></Link></Button>`. Separately, either define `.page-stack` in globals.css (`display:grid;gap:24px;max-width:1180px`) or delete the class from all three usages so no future page inherits a dead hook.

top_findings.title: Six two-column grids never set align-items:start, leaving large voids inside cards on connected home and settings
top_findings.problem: `.connected-main-grid` (2877), `.settings-grid` (1809), `.briefing-grid` (599), `.bottom-grid` (953), `.desk-layout` (1610) and `.connected-foundation-grid` (3007) all default to `align-items: stretch`, so the shorter card is pulled to the taller card's height. Compounded on the connected home by `app/globals.css:2979` `.connected-desk > [data-slot="button"] { margin-top: auto; }`, which pins the CTA to the bottom of the stretched card. cdesktop-home.png shows roughly 300px of empty card between "Your desk is clear." and "Add an idea or request". cdesktop-settings.png shows "The creative firewall" card stretched to match a four-card right column, leaving about 700px of dead space. Both read as rendering failures rather than as breathing room. components/kira/library.css:8 already sets `align-items: start` on `.library-detail-grid`, so the fix is known good in this codebase.
top_findings.proposed_change: Add `align-items: start;` to all six grid rules; remove `margin-top: auto` from `.connected-desk > [data-slot="button"]` (line 2980) and give `.connected-desk` `display:grid; gap:18px;` so the button follows its content.

top_findings.title: The consent checkbox and the manuscript file picker are unstyled browser defaults
top_findings.problem: `.library-check input[type=checkbox]` sets only `accent-color: #b3a68f`, which affects nothing in the unchecked state, so "I have permission to upload this manuscript and have Kira's AI services analyze it privately" is preceded by a bright white OS square on a near-black page — visible in both cdesktop- and cmobile-universe-assassins-refusal.png. Immediately above it, line 15 leaves `input[type=file]` as a raw `Choose File | No file chosen` in the system font. The same white-square problem appears fifteen times at once on cdesktop-plans.png via `components/kira/plans.css:1` `.plan-options input{accent-color:#d8ac6b}`, and again in `.studio-book-selection input` (app/globals.css:3688). The single most consequential act of trust in the product — handing over her novel — is presented with the least designed controls in the product.
top_findings.proposed_change: Add one shared custom-checkbox rule in globals.css using `appearance:none` with a 20px box, `1.5px solid var(--input)`, `--gold` fill and a CSS checkmark on `:checked`, applied to `.library-check input[type=checkbox]`, `.plan-options input[type=checkbox]`, `.studio-book-selection input[type=checkbox]` and `.ads-compare-toggle input`. Frame the consent row itself (`padding:16px; border:1px solid var(--input); border-radius:8px`, gold border when checked) and style the file input as a 96px dashed drop target with a styled `::file-selector-button`.

top_findings.title: There is no type scale: 48 distinct font sizes, an 8px default eyebrow with 5–7px overrides, and a 10px default link
top_findings.problem: `.eyebrow` — used 113 times across 28 components — is 8px uppercase at 0.17em tracking, and eighteen selectors shrink it further: `.recommendation-top .eyebrow` and `.agent-state` to 6px (lines 880, 996), `.cover-placeholder` to 5px (1453), and the mobile block drops `.agent-state` and `.cover-placeholder` to 5px (2034, 2211). `.text-link`, the product's standard inline link, is 10px (line 846) with no minimum target — below WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8's 24×24 floor. On the connected home the supporting copy is 11px (2966, 2975) and 9px (2874, 3066) beside a 45px serif number (2865). Across all four stylesheets there are 48 distinct font sizes, including 3px, 4px, 5px, 6px and 7px. A comment at line 2699 — "Legibility refinements for compact editorial surfaces" — followed by four one-off bumps shows the problem was noticed and patched per-component rather than fixed at the scale.
top_findings.proposed_change: Define a six-step scale on `:root` (`--text-xs:12px; --text-sm:13px; --text-base:15px; --text-lg:17px;` plus the existing display clamps), set `body` to 15px (from 13px, line 71), raise `.eyebrow` to 11px at 0.12em tracking and delete all eighteen shrink overrides, raise `.text-link` to 13px with `min-height:24px` (44px under 760px) and an underline, and raise the connected-home caption sizes to 12–14px. Leave the display sizes alone — the Cormorant hierarchy is the best thing in the product.

top_findings.title: Error and loading states on /opportunities, /plans and the global boundary are unstyled text with no recovery control nearby
top_findings.problem:
`{error&&

{error}

}` renders "Your book library could not complete that request. Your saved work is still here." as a bare body-coloured sentence on an otherwise empty page, with the only Refresh button 100px away in the top-right (cdesktop-opportunities.png). Loading is `

Checking approved book knowledge…

` — no skeleton, despite `app/loading.tsx` proving the pattern exists. `app/error.tsx:5` and `app/not-found.tsx:5` both reuse `.empty-state`, a dashed 75px-padded box (app/globals.css:1783) that also renders "Your desk is clear." and "A clean slate." — so a crash and a success look identical. `.empty-state p` is 12px (1799) under a 38px heading.
top_findings.proposed_change: Add a `.failure-state` in globals.css distinct from `.empty-state`: solid `1px solid var(--destructive)`, `background:#2a1a1e`, `TriangleAlert` icon, `p{font-size:15px;max-width:46ch}`. Use it in app/error.tsx and for the opportunities and plans error branches, always with the retry control inside the block. Replace the bare loading paragraphs with `<Skeleton>` rows. Raise `.empty-state p` to 15px.

top_findings.title: The connected home's only numbers read "08 · 00 · 00 · 00" with no empty-state treatment
top_findings.problem: `{count.known ? String(count.value).padStart(2, "0") : "—"}` renders zero-padded values at 45px Cormorant (app/globals.css:2865). For a brand-new workspace — exactly Cassy's state tomorrow — three of the four tiles show "00", so the largest, most prominent numeric element on her home page is a row of zeros with 9px captions beneath. It also reads as a bug rather than a fact, since "00" is an unusual way to write none. The strip is the only chrome-less block on a page otherwise made of cards, so it floats without belonging to either grid above or below it.
top_findings.proposed_change: Render `0` as an em-dash or a short phrase rather than "00" — e.g. `{!count.known ? "—" : count.value === 0 ? "—" : String(count.value).padStart(2,"0")}` with the caption carrying the meaning ("Nothing yet" / "Your reviewed history"). Raise the caption sizes to 12px, and either give `.connected-overview` the same `var(--card)` background and border radius as the cards around it or drop the border entirely so it reads deliberately as a rule-separated strip.

top_findings.title: The connected Marketing Plans form is the one page that looks like unstyled admin software
top_findings.problem: cdesktop-plans.png shows fifteen default white checkboxes, two native `<select>` elements with OS chrome, a `mm/dd/yyyy` date field with the browser calendar glyph, and labels at 13px — inside a page that also nests a card ("Build a plan") containing fieldsets that look like cards. `.plans-page` also runs its own focus ring (`outline:2px solid #d8ac6b`) and its own hover accent (`#d8ac6b`) rather than `var(--gold)`, and `.plan-row span` picks a third gold. It is the densest page in the product and visibly the one that received the least design attention.
top_findings.proposed_change: Route `.plans-page input:not([type=checkbox]), .plans-page select, .plans-page textarea` through the same rule that already styles `.connection-form select, .access-role-select, .studio-form select` (app/globals.css:3495) so all three form families match; apply the shared custom checkbox; replace `#d8ac6b` with `var(--gold)` throughout plans.css; and flatten the nesting by turning `.plan-options` fieldsets into bordered groups with a `.eyebrow` legend instead of card-like boxes inside a card.

top_findings.title: "The minions are working. Go write. 🖤" — the only emoji and the only diminutive in the product, and it claims work that is not happening
top_findings.problem: This string renders in the demo empty state on both the home page and the desk (duplicated at components/kira/desk-page.tsx:111). It is the only emoji in a visual system built on Cormorant Garamond, hairline gold rules and 0.17em uppercase eyebrows, so it lands as a different author's voice. It also states that background agents are working, which components/kira/agent-status.tsx:50 explicitly denies further down the same page ("Specialists are foundations, not running agents"). No e2e test pins this string — I grepped tests/ for "minions" and found nothing.
top_findings.proposed_change: Replace both occurrences with `Nothing needs you right now. Go write.` — same warmth, same brevity, no false status, no emoji.

top_findings.title: 532 hardcoded hex values against 123 token references; five checkbox accents and six focus-ring colours
top_findings.problem: Across globals.css, plans.css, library.css and ads/dashboard.css there are 532 distinct colour literals and only 123 `var(--…)` uses. `--card: #191a18` exists but `.settings-card` hardcodes `#1b1f16` (line 1816), `.connected-catalog` `#1b1f18` (3011), `.ads-panel` `#171c16`, `.connected-desk` `#1d1c18` (2947) — four different card surfaces. `--gold: #c7af83` exists but plans.css uses `#d8ac6b`, ads uses `#cbb991`/`#d0bb8e`/`#f0d79f`, library uses `#b9a68b`/`#dbccba`. Focus rings appear in six colours across five files; checkbox `accent-color` in five. The four `--radius-*` tokens at lines 52–55 are never referenced while ten literal radii are in use.
top_findings.proposed_change: Do a mechanical token pass: map every card surface to `var(--card)`, every gold accent to `var(--gold)`, every border to `var(--border)`/`var(--input)`, every muted caption to `var(--muted-foreground)`, and every radius to the existing `--radius-*` tokens. Delete the per-file focus-ring overrides so `a/button/summary:focus-visible` at line 96 governs everywhere. This is largely find-and-replace and will not change any rendered string, so no e2e test is at risk.

top_findings.title: Mobile catalog filters are 9px buttons with a 1px gap
top_findings.problem: Under the mobile breakpoint `.catalog-filters { gap: 1px }` and its buttons drop to `font-size: 9px; padding-inline: 8px`. In mobile-universe.png the four series toggles ("All titles 8", "My Alpha Team", "Assassin of Onisea", "Ambros Triplets") sit as a cramped row of near-illegible ghost labels with effectively no separation between adjacent tap targets. These are `aria-pressed` toggles, so both size and spacing fall under WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8. It is also the primary way to navigate her own catalog on a phone.
top_findings.proposed_change: Change the mobile override to `gap: 8px` and the button override to `font-size: 12px; padding-inline: 12px; min-height: 40px`, and let the row wrap to two lines rather than compressing.

top_findings.title: Fourteen breakpoints across four stylesheets with no shared system
top_findings.problem: globals.css declares media queries at 1550, 1250, 1020, 760, 380, 1100, 900, 600, 760, 1100, 640, 761+920h, 640 and 760; plans.css adds 700; library.css adds 800, 1000 and 700; ads/dashboard.css adds 1050 and 650. That is fourteen distinct widths at which some part of the layout reflows. Between 650 and 760, for example, the ads page has already collapsed to a single column while the desktop sidebar is still shown and buttons have not yet received their 44px mobile minimum (app/globals.css:3680). Nothing is broken at the two widths that were screenshotted, but the layout has no predictable behaviour between them.
top_findings.proposed_change: Consolidate to four breakpoints — 640, 768, 1024, 1440 — declared once as a comment block at the top of globals.css, and migrate the per-file queries in plans.css, library.css and ads/dashboard.css onto them. Worth doing as a follow-up pass rather than tonight, since it touches layout everywhere and needs visual re-checking at several widths.
top_findings.owner_decision_needed: None, but this is the one item I would schedule after tomorrow's demo rather than before it — it is the highest-risk change on this list and the lowest visible payoff.

top_findings.title: Editors cannot approve a marketing plan, and the UI tells her so in one line of grey text naming a man
top_findings.problem:
`{role!=="owner"&&plan.status==="needs_review"&&

Michael can review this plan and activate its tasks. You can keep exploring while it awaits review.

}` — while the owner branch at line 103 gets a full `Owner review` card with a notes textarea and three buttons. Cassy is an Editor. She can build the entire plan and then receives a small grey sentence telling her a named person will decide. The asymmetry in visual weight makes the limit feel like a status judgement rather than a workspace setting, and there is nothing she can click.
top_findings.proposed_change: Give the non-owner state a card of equal weight: heading "Waiting on owner review", body explaining that plan activation is a workspace access setting rather than a limit on her account, and a `View who can review` button linking to /access. Separately, at line 50, stop silently hiding the whole "Build a plan" card from viewers — render a short explanatory card in its place, as manual-review-form.tsx:130 and approval-card.tsx:143 already do.
top_findings.owner_decision_needed: Whether an Editor should be able to approve and activate her own marketing plans at all is Michael's call and I am not proposing to change it. How that gate is explained, and whether it has equal visual weight and a route forward, is code and should be fixed either way.

what_works: The display typography. Cormorant Garamond at clamp(38px, 3.4vw, 56px) with -0.045em tracking and 1.04 line-height (app/globals.css:118-122), broken across two lines with the second line italic and gold via `h1 em { color: #cfbd9e }` (line 123). "Good afternoon, Cassandra." / "They bring the evidence. You bring the instinct." / "A few ground rules. Beautifully nonnegotiable." — this is the product's signature and it is genuinely distinctive. Do not flatten it while fixing the small type.

The login and welcome stage (app/login/page.tsx:25-55, app/welcome/page.tsx:20-37). Full-bleed dark, a hero column with the brand mark, the two-line serif hero, the "Let Kira write." mantra with a feather, and a real Brontë epigraph sourced to Project Gutenberg — against a single quiet card. It is the most confident screen in the product and needs nothing.

The book covers (desktop-universe.png, mobile-universe.png). Eight generated placeholder covers in plum, sage and slate with a double inner rule, a small diamond-and-star device, the title in Cormorant and "CATALOG PLACEHOLDER · NOT OFFICIAL COVER" set honestly into the artwork. Honest provenance rendered as decoration rather than as a disclaimer. This is the best single piece of craft in the codebase.

The RavenArt SVG (components/kira/raven-art.tsx). A constellation-line raven at 6-14% opacity behind the briefing card, with orbit rings and registration ticks. Restrained, editorial, never cute. Keep the opacity where it is.

The demo Mission Control composition (components/kira/mission-control.tsx:31-169). Six metric cards with sparklines, an asymmetric 2.15fr/1fr briefing row, a three-up moves grid, the plum inspiration panel, then a two-up foundation row. The rhythm of eyebrow → serif h2 → body → action repeats cleanly down the page. This is the page the others should be measured against.

The provenance badge system (components/kira/origin-badge.tsx, `.origin-badge` / `.origin-demo` / `.origin-manual`). Small, consistent, never apologetic, and present on every synthetic number including inside the metric cards' sr-only text (metric-card.tsx:42). Do not weaken this while raising font sizes — raise the badge to 10px rather than removing it.

The mobile input and button floor (app/globals.css:3674-3686): 16px font on all inputs to prevent iOS zoom, 44px minimum height on inputs, selects and every button, textarea line-height relaxed to 1.65, and `white-space: normal` with auto height on the buttons most likely to wrap. This is real, deliberate mobile work and the type-scale fixes must not undo it.

Focus management around dialogs (components/kira/approval-card.tsx:167-175, app-shell.tsx:417-419). `onOpenAutoFocus` sends focus to Cancel on destructive dialogs rather than to the confirm button, and `onCloseAutoFocus` returns focus to the originating trigger or falls back to the Reviewed tab when the trigger has unmounted. That fallback is a detail most teams never get to.

`align-items: start` on `.library-detail-grid` (components/kira/library.css:8) and the mobile collapse block at lines 48-54. The library stylesheet is the one feature CSS file that behaves like a system; use it as the reference when fixing the other five grids.
The reduced-motion block (app/globals.css:2689-2697) neutralising `scroll-behavior: smooth` as well as animations and transitions — the smooth-scroll reset is the part usually forgotten.

The empty-state copy itself, separate from its styling: "Your desk is clear.", "A clean slate.", "A place for this book's memory.", "Your first question will appear here when you ask. Nothing runs in the background." These are warm and honest. Only the containers need work.
